label: Air Quality
summary: Poor air quality happens when smoke, pollution, or fumes build up outdoors or indoors. It can make breathing harder, especially for children, older adults, and people with heart or lung conditions.

items.label: Follow local alerts
items.body: When the Air Quality Index (AQI) is above 100, limit time and hard activity outdoors, especially if you have a higher risk.

items.label: Keep windows closed when outdoor air is unhealthy
items.body: A well-fitting N95 or KN95 mask can help if you must be outside.

items.label: Install carbon monoxide alarms
items.body: Never run a generator indoors or use a stove for heat.

items.label: Trouble breathing, chest pain, or a carbon monoxide alarm sounding?
items.body: Move to fresh air and call 911.

items.label: Prepare for poor air quality days
items.body: AQI levels, clean-air spaces, air filters and purifiers, and masks.

items.label: Learn how air pollution affects health
items.body: Common pollutants, who is most at risk, and ways to reduce exposure.

items.label: Prevent carbon monoxide poisoning
items.body: Alarm and fuel-burning appliance safety. If an alarm sounds or poisoning is suspected, leave and call 911.

items.label: Check current air quality
items.body: From the U.S. EPA: current AQI and forecast for your location. Spanish resources available.

items.label: Check the New York State air quality forecast
items.body: Daily forecast and Air Quality Health Advisories. Air Quality Hotline: 800-535-1345.

items.label: Protect yourself from smoke and high ozone
items.body: What to do at each AQI level, masks, and portable air cleaners. Translated AQI and mask guidance.

items.label: Report an indoor air quality problem
items.body: Dust, chemical odors, soot, or poor ventilation in your building. Anonymous reports accepted for most issues.

items.label: Know when to leave or stay inside
items.body: Evacuation and shelter-in-place guidance. Follow instructions for the specific emergency.
